framework.name: Security Practices Evaluation
framework.description: Comprehensive security audit framework for the FGC Upper Room platform. Covers authentication, authorization, secrets management, input validation, session handling, cryptography, error handling, and secure defaults across the full stack: Vite/React frontend, Express.js backend services (WhatsApp Bot port 4100, Attendance Service port 4201), PostgreSQL database, Redis/BullMQ, and Cloudflare Tunnel deployment.

rubric.1-2: Critical: Actively exploitable vulnerability present. Immediate remediation required.
rubric.3-4: Poor: Major security gaps. Missing fundamental controls.
rubric.5-6: Fair: Some controls in place but significant gaps remain.
rubric.7-8: Good: Solid security posture with minor improvements needed.
rubric.9-10: Excellent: Industry best practices implemented and verified.

scoring.overall_calculation: Weighted average of all category scores. Categories weighted by risk impact.

categories.name: Authentication & Identity
categories.description: How users prove their identity to the system. Covers the admin login system, session tokens, 2FA/TOTP, and any public-facing authentication flows.

criteria.name: Password Storage
what_to_check: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost >= 12), Argon2, or scrypt — never MD5, SHA-256 alone, or plaintext
Check admin user JSON files and any DB tables for password field handling
Verify salt is unique per user (bcrypt does this automatically)
No password is ever logged, returned in API responses, or stored in localStorage/sessionStorage
known_issues: Previous audit found VITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD baked into the JS bundle via Vite env vars
Fallback login bypass pattern (getFallbackLogin / fallback-local-admin) was discovered
Phase 1 removed VITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD and fallback login — verify removal is complete and no remnants exist in git history or dist/
criteria.remediation: Use bcrypt with cost factor 12+. Remove all VITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD references. Eliminate any fallback/bypass login paths. Server-side only password verification.

criteria.name: Session Management
what_to_check: Session tokens are cryptographically random (crypto.randomBytes, not Math.random)
Tokens have expiration (recommend 1-4 hours for admin sessions)
Sessions are invalidated on logout (server-side deletion, not just client cookie removal)
Session fixation prevention: new token issued after successful login
Cookie flags: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict or Lax
No session tokens stored in localStorage (XSS-accessible)
known_issues: Admin system uses JSON files on disk for session storage — verify token generation quality
Admin sessions still use JSON files on disk (data/admin-sessions.json) — verify this wasn't migrated to PostgreSQL in Phase 2 (it wasn't — still a gap)
criteria.remediation: Use crypto.randomBytes(32) for tokens. Set all cookie security flags. Implement server-side session store with TTL. Regenerate session ID on authentication state change.

criteria.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
what_to_check: TOTP 2FA is enforced for super_admin role, recommended for editor/reviewer
TOTP secrets are stored encrypted or in a secure location, not plaintext JSON
Backup/recovery codes exist for 2FA lockout scenarios
TOTP window is limited (1-2 periods, not unlimited)
criteria.remediation: Encrypt TOTP secrets at rest. Implement backup codes. Enforce 2FA for all admin roles.

criteria.name: Brute Force Protection
what_to_check: Login endpoints have rate limiting (e.g., 5 attempts per 15 minutes per IP/account)
Account lockout or exponential backoff after repeated failures
Failed login attempts are logged with timestamp and IP
Rate limiting applies to password reset flows too
criteria.remediation: Use express-rate-limit on /login, /reset-password. Implement progressive delays. Log all auth failures to audit log.

categories.name: Authorization & Access Control
categories.description: What authenticated users can do. Covers RBAC enforcement, route protection, and data-level access controls.

criteria.name: RBAC Enforcement
what_to_check: Every admin route checks user role server-side before executing
Role checks happen in middleware, not just in route handlers (defense in depth)
Roles are defined: super_admin, editor, reviewer — verify each has correct permissions
No routes rely solely on client-side role checks (React component visibility)
Default deny: if role is unknown/missing, access is denied
known_issues: Need to verify all bot admin endpoints (events, visitors, messages) require role checks
criteria.remediation: Create a central authorization middleware. Apply it to ALL admin routes. Implement permission matrix: which role can access which endpoints.

criteria.name: API Endpoint Protection
what_to_check: ALL write endpoints (POST/PUT/DELETE) require authentication
Bot admin API endpoints verify x-bot-admin-key or session token
Attendance service endpoints that modify data require auth
Public read endpoints are intentionally public (not accidentally unprotected)
Document which endpoints are public vs. authenticated vs. admin-only
known_issues: Previous audit found unauthenticated bot write endpoints
criteria.remediation: Audit every route in bot/src/routes/ and attendance service. Add auth middleware to all state-changing endpoints. Create an endpoint inventory with auth requirements.

criteria.name: Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR)
what_to_check: Users cannot access other users' data by modifying IDs in URLs/params
Attendance check-in records are scoped to the correct session
Visitor/member records are only accessible by authorized admin roles
Prayer requests and feedback are not publicly enumerable
criteria.remediation: Always scope queries by the authenticated user's permissions. Use UUIDs instead of sequential IDs for external-facing references.

categories.name: Secrets & Configuration Management
categories.description: How sensitive credentials, API keys, and configuration values are stored and accessed.

criteria.name: No Hardcoded Secrets
what_to_check: grep -r for patterns: password, secret, api_key, token, credential in source files
No secrets in .env files committed to git (check .gitignore)
No VITE_ prefixed env vars exposing secrets to the client bundle
WhatsApp Cloud API token stored in env vars, not source
PostgreSQL connection strings use env vars
Redis connection credentials use env vars
LLM API keys (Vertex AI, OpenAI, Gemini) use env vars
Paystack keys are implemented — verify PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY is server-side only, with test vs live separation
known_issues: VITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD was removed in Phase 1 — verify no VITE_ prefixed secrets remain
Paystack is now implemented — verify PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY is server-side only (never in frontend bundle)
criteria.remediation: Remove ALL secrets from source. Use dotenv for local dev, proper secret management for production. Audit git history for previously committed secrets (they need rotation even after removal). Never use VITE_ prefix for secrets.

criteria.name: Environment Separation
what_to_check: Separate .env files or configs for development, staging, production
Production secrets are NOT in the git repository, even in .env.example
Example env file (.env.example) has placeholder values only
NODE_ENV is set correctly per environment
criteria.remediation: Create .env.example with dummy values. Use .env.local for dev. Production uses server-level env vars or secret manager.

criteria.name: Secret Rotation Readiness
what_to_check: Can secrets (DB password, API keys, session secret) be rotated without downtime?
Is there a documented process for rotating compromised credentials?
WhatsApp API token refresh is handled (Meta tokens expire)
criteria.remediation: Document secret rotation procedures. Ensure app can reload config without restart where possible.

criteria.name: JSON File Data Store Security
what_to_check: data/admin-users.json (password hashes, TOTP secrets) has restricted file permissions (600 or 640)
data/admin-sessions.json is not committed to git (.gitignore covers data/ directory)
data/admin-audit-log.json is access-controlled
data/admin-blog-posts.json, data/admin-testimonies.json, data/admin-media.json — file permissions appropriate
data/contact-submissions.json, data/newsletter-subscribers.json — contain PII, verify permissions
data/rum-events.json — assess sensitivity
All data/*.json files are excluded from git via .gitignore
Concurrent write safety: JSON file writes use atomic write pattern (write to temp, rename) to prevent corruption
Migration plan exists to move remaining JSON stores to PostgreSQL (same pattern as giving migration)
known_issues: Giving data was migrated from JSON to PostgreSQL in Phase 3, but all other data stores remain as flat JSON files
JSON file storage has concurrency and data loss risks that were the motivation for the giving migration
criteria.remediation: Set file permissions to 600 for sensitive files (admin-users, admin-sessions). Ensure data/ is in .gitignore. Plan incremental migration to PostgreSQL. Use atomic writes (fs.writeFile to temp path + fs.rename) to prevent corruption.

categories.name: Input Validation & Output Encoding
categories.description: How the application handles untrusted data from users, WhatsApp messages, and external APIs.

criteria.name: Server-Side Input Validation
what_to_check: All API endpoints validate incoming data (type, length, format, range)
Use express-validator, Joi, Zod, or equivalent — not just manual checks
WhatsApp webhook payload is validated against Meta's expected schema
Attendance check-in data (member ID, session ID) is validated
Event creation/update validates all fields (dates, capacity, text lengths)
Contact form and subscription endpoints validate email format, sanitize message text
criteria.remediation: Add validation middleware to every endpoint. Define schemas for all input types. Reject invalid input with 400 status and safe error messages.

criteria.name: SQL Injection Prevention
what_to_check: ALL PostgreSQL queries use parameterized queries ($1, $2) or an ORM
No string concatenation to build SQL queries
Search/filter functionality uses parameterized LIKE queries
Check visitor duplicate detection queries, event queries, attendance queries
criteria.remediation: Use parameterized queries everywhere. Use pg library's query(text, values) pattern. Consider an ORM like Knex for complex queries.

criteria.name: XSS Prevention
what_to_check: React JSX auto-escaping is relied upon (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML without DOMPurify)
Blog content, testimonies, and user-generated text are sanitized before storage AND display
Rich text/HTML content uses DOMPurify or equivalent
URL parameters are not reflected unsanitized into page content
Event descriptions and prayer requests are sanitized
known_issues: Blog and testimony content was migrated from localStorage to server-side JSON files (data/admin-blog-posts.json, data/admin-testimonies.json) — ensure sanitization on both write and read paths
criteria.remediation: Audit all dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage. Add DOMPurify for any HTML rendering. Sanitize on input AND output.

criteria.name: WhatsApp Message Input Handling
what_to_check: Inbound WhatsApp messages are sanitized before processing
Command parsing (@email, STOP, FAQ triggers) handles edge cases and injection
LLM prompt injection: user messages passed to Vertex AI/OpenAI/Gemini are sandboxed
Message content stored in PostgreSQL is parameterized
Opt-out parsing doesn't execute arbitrary commands
criteria.remediation: Sanitize all inbound message text. Use strict regex for command parsing. Sandbox LLM inputs with system prompts that instruct ignoring injected instructions.

categories.name: Cryptography & Data Protection
categories.description: Encryption in transit and at rest, secure random number generation, and data protection.

criteria.name: HTTPS / TLS
what_to_check: All traffic served over HTTPS (Cloudflare Tunnel handles this)
No mixed content (HTTP resources loaded on HTTPS pages)
HSTS headers present
Internal service-to-service communication (bot <-> attendance) is secured
criteria.remediation: Verify Cloudflare Tunnel enforces HTTPS. Add HSTS header. Check internal service communication.

criteria.name: Secure Randomness
what_to_check: All tokens, session IDs, and security-sensitive values use crypto.randomBytes or crypto.randomUUID
No Math.random() for security purposes (tokens, IDs, codes)
QR code generation uses secure random identifiers
TOTP implementation uses proper cryptographic library
criteria.remediation: Replace any Math.random() in security contexts with crypto module equivalents.

criteria.name: Data Encryption at Rest
what_to_check: Sensitive data in PostgreSQL (phone numbers, prayer requests, personal info) — assess if encryption is needed
Admin JSON files with password hashes and TOTP secrets — are these on encrypted filesystem?
Backup files are encrypted
Redis data (queued messages, session cache) — assess sensitivity
criteria.remediation: For a church website, column-level encryption may be overkill, but ensure filesystem permissions are tight and backups are encrypted. Document the decision.

categories.name: HTTP Security Headers & Middleware
categories.description: Security headers and Express middleware hardening.

criteria.name: Helmet.js Usage
what_to_check: helmet() middleware is applied to all Express apps (bot, attendance, any API server)
Content-Security-Policy is configured (not just default)
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is set
X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN is set
X-Powered-By header is removed (helmet does this)
criteria.remediation: Install and configure helmet() on every Express app. Customize CSP for your needs.

criteria.name: CORS Configuration
what_to_check: CORS is configured to allow only your domain(s), not wildcard *
Credentials mode is properly set if using cookies cross-origin
Preflight requests are handled correctly
Bot webhook endpoint CORS allows Meta's servers
known_issues: Phase 3 added CORS whitelist to giving API — verify it covers all API routes, not just giving
criteria.remediation: Set CORS origin to your specific domains. Use cors() middleware with explicit origin list.

criteria.name: Rate Limiting
what_to_check: express-rate-limit applied to public-facing endpoints
Different rate limits for different endpoint types (auth = strict, public = moderate)
Bot webhook has appropriate limits (Meta may send bursts)
Attendance check-in has rate limiting (already noted as present)
known_issues: Phase 3 added rate limiting to /api/giving/initialize (10 req/min/IP) — verify other public endpoints (contact form, newsletter subscribe, attendance check-in) also have rate limiting
criteria.remediation: Apply tiered rate limiting: auth endpoints (5/15min), API endpoints (100/15min), webhooks (appropriate for Meta's patterns).

categories.name: Error Handling & Information Disclosure
categories.description: How errors are handled, logged, and communicated to users.

criteria.name: No Stack Traces in Responses
what_to_check: Production error responses return generic messages, not stack traces
Express error handler middleware catches all unhandled errors
No err.stack or err.message directly sent to client in production
Database errors (PostgreSQL) are caught and not leaked to client
criteria.remediation: Implement global error handler middleware on every Express app. Return generic 500 messages. Log full errors server-side only.

criteria.name: Secure Logging
what_to_check: Logs do not contain passwords, tokens, API keys, or full credit card numbers
Logs do not contain full WhatsApp message content from users (privacy)
Log levels are appropriate (debug off in production)
Structured logging format for easy analysis
criteria.remediation: Audit all logger.info/warn/error calls. Redact sensitive fields. Use structured logging (winston or pino).

criteria.name: Graceful Shutdown & Error Recovery
what_to_check: SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers exist for clean shutdown
Database connections are closed on shutdown
Redis connections are closed on shutdown
BullMQ workers are drained before exit
Process doesn't crash on unhandled promise rejections (process.on('unhandledRejection'))
known_issues: Phase 1 added SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers to all three services — verify they actually work (drain connections, close pools, 15-second timeout)
criteria.remediation: Add process signal handlers. Drain queues. Close DB/Redis pools. Set process.on('unhandledRejection') to log and handle.

categories.name: Dependency Security
categories.description: Third-party package security and supply chain risk.

criteria.name: Known Vulnerability Scan
what_to_check: Run npm audit on all package.json files (frontend, bot, attendance)
No high or critical vulnerabilities in direct dependencies
Dependabot or similar is enabled on the GitHub repo
Lock files (package-lock.json) are committed and up to date
criteria.remediation: Run npm audit fix. Enable GitHub Dependabot alerts. Pin dependency versions. Review and update quarterly.

criteria.name: Dependency Hygiene
what_to_check: No unused packages in package.json (depcheck tool)
No deprecated packages still in use
Minimal dependencies — no unnecessary packages adding attack surface
LLM-related packages are from official/verified sources
criteria.remediation: Run npx depcheck. Remove unused deps. Replace deprecated packages.

categories.name: WhatsApp-Specific Security
categories.description: Security controls specific to the WhatsApp Bot integration via Meta Cloud API.

criteria.name: Webhook Verification
what_to_check: Webhook endpoint verifies Meta's signature (X-Hub-Signature-256 header)
Webhook verify token is checked on GET requests (Meta's challenge verification)
Webhook endpoint only processes verified payloads
Replay protection: check message timestamps aren't stale
criteria.remediation: Implement X-Hub-Signature-256 verification middleware. Verify the shared secret matches. Reject unsigned or invalid payloads.

criteria.name: Opt-Out & Privacy
what_to_check: STOP/opt-out is respected immediately and persisted
Opted-out numbers do not receive any further messages
Member phone numbers are stored securely
Message history retention policy exists (don't store indefinitely without reason)
criteria.remediation: Verify opt-out flow end-to-end. Implement data retention policy. Consider hashing phone numbers at rest.

criteria.name: LLM Message Safety
what_to_check: LLM-generated messages are reviewed/templated, not raw model output sent to users
System prompts prevent the LLM from generating harmful, off-topic, or inappropriate content
Fallback to static templates when LLM fails (cascading provider strategy)
LLM responses are length-limited and content-filtered before sending
criteria.remediation: Add output validation on LLM responses. Ensure system prompts are restrictive. Test with adversarial inputs.

criteria.name: Giving Notification Security
what_to_check: /bot/api/giving/notify endpoint validates BOT_ADMIN_API_KEY in request header before processing
Endpoint cannot be spoofed to send arbitrary WhatsApp messages (only sends pre-defined thank-you template)
Donor PII (name, email, amount) is not leaked in server logs when notification is sent
Thank-you message respects opt-out status (does not message opted-out numbers)
Fire-and-forget pattern from website API to bot logs failures (not silently dropped)
Notification payload is validated (phone number format, transaction reference exists)
known_issues: Phase 3 added /bot/api/giving/notify as internal endpoint — verify BOT_ADMIN_API_KEY check is present and correct
Fire-and-forget from website to bot may silently drop failures — verify error logging
criteria.remediation: Verify BOT_ADMIN_API_KEY middleware on /bot/api/giving/notify. Check opt-out status before sending thank-you. Log notification failures with transaction reference (but not donor PII). Validate payload schema.

evaluation_instructions.for_claude_code: To evaluate this framework against the codebase, read this JSON file, then systematically check each criterion against the actual source code. For each criterion: 1) Search the codebase for relevant files and patterns, 2) Score 1-10 based on the rubric, 3) Document specific file paths and line numbers as evidence, 4) Note any findings that match known_issues, 5) Provide actionable remediation steps with code examples where possible. Output a markdown report to evaluation/results/ with timestamp.

sections: Executive Summary (overall score, critical findings count)
Category Scores (table with category, score, weight, weighted score)
Detailed Findings (per criterion: score, evidence, files, remediation)
Progress Tracking (comparison with previous evaluation if exists)
